words.gloss: to those who do not have
it is as if they have nothing

literal: Giving and enjoying to those who do not have, piled-up crores though there are, nothing.
translation: To those who neither give to others nor enjoy their wealth themselves, even if they possess piled-up crores of riches, they actually have nothing.
modern: பிறருக்குக் கொடுப்பதும் தாம் அனுபவிப்பதும் இல்லாதவர்க்கு, அடுக்கடுக்கான கோடிப் பொருள்கள் இருந்தாலும் அதனால் ஒரு பயனும் இல்லை.
explanation: This couplet highlights the futility of hoarded wealth that is neither shared nor enjoyed. The poet uses the words 'கொடுப்பதூஉம்' (giving) and 'துய்ப்பதூஉம்' (enjoying) with poetic elongation to emphasize these two essential purposes of wealth. For those who lack both these actions, having even piled-up crores ('அடுக்கிய கோடி') of riches is equivalent to having nothing ('இல்'). True wealth is defined by its utility and generosity, not by its mere accumulation.
